To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
18 BrrMTP homologs were identified from the turnip (Brassica rapa) genome, and the expression profiles of these genes under diverse metal ion stress conditions were determined.
18 candidate Cation diffusion facilitator genes were identified from the turnip and their potential roles were discussed.
we have identified 18 candidate BrrMTP family members in turnip and performed a comprehensive analysis on the characteristics and functions of these genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of CDF gene family in turnip and provides a valuable resource for further functional analysis of BrrMPTs in response to metal ion stresses.
the identification, phylogenetic relationships and expression patterns of CDF genes in turnip.
the genome-wide identification of the BrrCDF family, which is the first report of this gene family in turnip.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CDF gene family in turnip is involved in the transport of Mg, Zn, Fe, Mn, Co, Cu, Na, and/or Cd, and the expression of most BrrMTP s is induced by at least a metal ion stress.
the CDF genes are involved in metal ion transport in plants, and their functions are diverse and complicated.
MTPs are involved in metal ion homeostasis, heavy metal tolerance, and possibly the salt tolerance of turnip.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

BrrMPT1.2, BrrMTP4, BrrMPT5, BrrMPTS, BrrMPS, BrrMPL2, and BrrMPL3 may be involved in the transport of Mg, Zn, and Cu, BrrMTC1, BrrMPC, and BrrMPB may be related to Fe, Mn, and Co, and BrrMTD may be involved in Na and Cd homeostasis.
the BrrCation Diffusion Facilitor genes are possibly involved not only in metal ion homeostasis but also in the tolerance of salt and heavy metals in plants.
the BrrMTPIs are possibly involved in the maintenance of metal ion homeostasis in plant cells, which may be associated with the tolerance of heavy metal stress and salt stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified a large number of CDF genes from turnip genome and analyzed their structural features and expression patterns under metal ion stresses.
BrrMPT1.1–1.4, 2.1–2.4, 3.1, 3.2, 5.1–5.4, 6.1, 6.2, 8.1, 8.2, and 9.1 are the candidate genes involved in the uptake and transport of metal ions in turnip.
the BrrCDF genes may play important roles in the uptake and/or homeostasis of various metal ions in turnip.
